parts.title: Sailing Courses
parts.transcript: S1: woman phones about sailing courses for her 13-yr-old son Jacob. Taster Day 22nd June (example). Two-day course: basic techniques; kids always sail with their allocated instructor (1); cost 65 pounds (2). Five-day course (125): sail alone from day 3; receive a certificate on the last/final day (3). Clothing: warm clothes; must wear shoes - no bare feet (4); bring extra waterproof trousers (5); must not wear jeans - get heavy when wet (6). The seaplane was discontinued last week and a hovercraft service is delayed, so the only current link is the old ferry (11=C). Coasts: golf - the south 18-hole course is being turned into a conference centre, but two courses are on the east coast (12=C); large resorts & hotels with children's clubs are in the south (13=B); basic apartment complexes with kitchens (self-catering) are on the east coast (14=C); guided jungle treks/nature on the north coast (west rainforest inaccessible) (15=A). parts.transcript: S3: business student Laura and her tutor discuss research on employee absence at Burock (audio: Burcock) Engineering. She picked it because the managing director got in touch with her (her old FG contact's CEO referred her) (21=A; placement & known staff were at FG). Tutor advises not to be that specific - look at absence as a whole, so she broadens the focus (22=B). She expects to find absence is related to the type of job the employee does (23=A; rises rejected, unjustified-absence hard to determine). From records she can get anonymous details like type of work / length of service = details of employment (24=B; no DOB, no individual absence). Questionnaire recommendations: provide a mixture of question types (closed + open-ended) (C) and trial it on at least one person before finalising (E) (25/26=C,E; 'keep to minimum' wrong - tutor wants balance). Covering letter: explain it's voluntary/won't be used to assess them (B) and roughly how long it takes (C) (27/28=B,C). Definite dates already fixed: completion of the assignment (by the 2nd) (A) and the next tutor meeting (two weeks today) (D) (29/30=A,D; distribution/collection/analysis dates not yet set).

parts.title: Transhumance
parts.transcript: S4: lecture on transhumance (pastoralists moving with herds), fixed vs nomadic. Fixed (e.g. Switzerland, predictable seasons) movement pattern = vertical (31, low ground in winter to high in summer); nomadic (e.g. Somalia) is complex/varied. Homes: fixed have a semi-permanent mountain shelter such as a cabin (32); nomadic carry portable homes - the Gabra in N Kenya carry the frame on a camel (33). People: in fixed only the young pastoralists who tend the herds travel (34); in nomadic the whole group moves. Diet/goods: valley-stayers may become farmers (35); they trade animals for grain (36); nomadic herds provide all needs - food and clothing (37). Algeria case: they traditionally help local farmers with the harvest (38); they live in tents (39) all year (so look nomadic) but use the same mountain passes yearly (look fixed) - best termed intermediate (40).
